name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPR-357 'Journeyman'
description:
The Kang-Petrov KPR-357 is a medium-frame double-action revolver chambered in .357 Magnum, designed as the revolver equivalent of their ubiquitous KP-19 — reliable, affordable, and available everywhere. The frame is carbon steel with a matte stainless finish, and the four-inch barrel is heavy-profile for improved accuracy and reduced muzzle flip. The cylinder also accepts .38 Special ammunition for practice and reduced-recoil applications.

The Journeyman is the revolver that security professionals carry when they prefer wheel guns over semi-automatics. The .357 Magnum round provides stopping power that exceeds 9mm and approaches .44 Magnum at close range, while the weapon's medium frame keeps it manageable for extended carry. The ability to load .38 Special for practice reduces training costs significantly — a practical consideration that Kang-Petrov highlights in their marketing.

Kang-Petrov produces the KPR-357 in the same factories that build the KP-19, applying the same philosophy of volume production and consistent quality. The result is a revolver that lacks the hand-fitted refinement of premium offerings but delivers dependable performance at a price point that working professionals can afford without wincing.

caliber: .357 Magnum / .38 Special
effective_range: 45 meters

magazine_capacity: 6 rounds (cylinder)

tactical_use: A versatile duty revolver offering .357 Magnum stopping power with the option of .38 Special for training and reduced-recoil situations. The heavy-profile barrel improves accuracy and reduces muzzle flip. Suitable for open carry by security professionals and personal defense. Reloading is slower than semi-automatics — speedloaders are standard equipment for serious carriers.
cultural_context: The Journeyman is the working person's magnum revolver. It lacks the drama of the Mauler and the prestige of higher-end offerings, but it performs its job without complaint. Among revolver carriers, the KPR-357 is respected as an honest weapon — no flash, no gimmick, just competence.
story_hooks: A Journeyman loaded with .38 Special wadcutters is used in what appears to be a training accident — but the forensics don't match any shooting range in the district.
Kang-Petrov is discontinuing the KPR-357 due to declining revolver sales. The announcement triggers a buying rush among loyalists who consider it the last affordable quality revolver.

physical_description.visual_profile: A no-nonsense medium-frame revolver with a purposeful, utilitarian silhouette. The heavy four-inch barrel dominates the profile, giving the weapon a front-heavy, grounded appearance despite modest overall length. The proportions suggest competence over flash—a tool built for work, not show.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 23.5 cm. Barrel length: 10.2 cm. Cylinder diameter: 3.8 cm. Height from grip to top of frame: 13 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial without being oppressive—0.96 kg translates to a revolver that settles reassuringly in the hand. The heavy barrel provides counterbalance, making it feel balanced during extended carry rather than muzzle-heavy. Recoil management is tactile and controlled.
physical_description.primary_material: Medium-grade carbon steel frame and cylinder, investment-cast for durability and consistency rather than hand-fitted perfection. The heavy barrel is hammer-forged steel, visible as a distinct section with slightly different surface character.
physical_description.finish: Matte stainless steel with a utilitarian, unpolished quality. Not bright or reflective—rather a soft, slightly granular gray-silver that shows handling marks and minor scuffs as evidence of real-world use. Factory-standard without custom refinement.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte stainless gray as primary. Trigger, hammer, and internal components in dark blued steel creating subtle contrast. Grip panels in industrial-grade black polymer with minimal ornamentation.
physical_description.grip_texture: Black synthetic polymer panels with a fine cross-hatched texture—functional grip security without aggressive serration. Slightly warm to touch, designed for extended carry without chafing. The backstrap is smooth-curved, promoting retention in both open and concealed carry contexts.
distinctive_features: Heavy-profile barrel with subtle longitudinal machine lines from manufacturing
Recessed cylinder charge holes allowing visual ammunition status check
Standard K-frame square notch rear sight (fixed, drift-adjustable)
Replaceable front sight post (blade type, dovetailed)
Cylinder release button positioned forward of trigger guard (standard Kang-Petrov ergonomics)
Visible cylinder rotation detents showing precise machining tolerances
Smooth trigger face with subtle radius, designed for consistent double-action pull
Chamber markings: '.357 MAG / .38 SPL' etched into barrel forcing cone
Minimal tool marks visible at frame/barrel junction—production-line consistency evident
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: KANG-PETROV ARMS stamped in clean block letters along the left side of the barrel. Below: 'KPR-357 JOURNEYMAN' and caliber designation. Serial number plate on right side of frame below cylinder. Small Kang-Petrov logo (interlocking K-P monogram) on grip panel.
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-new or well-maintained. Light handling marks on barrel and frame from carry and training. No active corrosion. Possibly minor cylinder wear from repeated loading. The matte finish ages gracefully, developing subtle patina rather than obvious aging.
